newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amcoal exports rise to 14.3 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Amcoal exports rise to 14.3 mln tonnes.

text.p: Anglo American Coal Corp said on Wednesday its coal exports increased slightly to 14.3 million tonnes from 14.1 million tonnes in the year to March 31.

But coal exports through the Richards Bay Coal Terminal fell 0.2 million tonnes to 58.7 million tonnes. The decline was mostly due to problems experienced by opencast producers in the first half of the year after abnormnally high rains.
Amcoal said the work to increase Richards Bay's capacity to 63 million tonnes per annum should be finished by June.
Sales to electricity utility Eskom rose 1.7 million tonnes to 31.7 million tonnes -- two million tonnes below budgeted levels.

"Amcoal remains seriously concerned at the lower levels of output at our Kriel and New Denmark collieries and steps have been taken to remedy these problem areas; there is evidence of progressive improvements in output at both of these mines," Amcoal chairman Dave Rankin said.

He added that if Eskom could achieve on an ongoing basis the 90 percent overall average availability at power stations that it managed in 1996, it would ultimately require up to 15 million tonnes of coal annually over and above current contracted tonnage levels at existing power stations.
"This will provide additional supply opportunities to the coal industry in South Africa and Amcoal intends to respond to any Eskom coal supply enquiries in this regard," Rankin said.
Amcoal's sales of coal and coke to the industrial and metallurgical sectors of the South African market rose 6.6 percent to 2.25 million tonnes.
Supply still exceeded demand in the world steel industry and this had resulted in price decrease for the current year.

"Steam coal contract prices concluded for 1997 reflect a mix of similar levels to those achieved in 1996 and reductions, related to the timing of individual negotiations. Accordingly, average U.S. dollar prices in 1997 are expected to be lower than those achieved in 1996," Amcoal said.
Amcoal also announced it had appointed James Campbell as new chairman, replacing Rankin.
Campbell is a director of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers Consolidated Ltd.
